children: RBI cancelled licences of five NBFCs while eight others surrendered registrations following business exits, mergers, dissolution or changes in regulatory status

The Reserve Bank of India has cancelled the certificates of registration of five non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), while eight others have surrendered their registrations for various business and regulatory reasons.

The RBI cancelled the licences of Dar's Financial Services, Rolta Holding and Finance Corporation, Vasudeo Securities, Parsoli Corporation and A C Choksi Financial Services, according to the central bank's release. The action comes as the central bank continues to review the regulatory status of NBFCs and their compliance with requirements governing non-banking financial institutions.

Among the eight companies that surrendered their registrations, Anupam Mercantile, Grand Motor and Finance, Sky Limit International Finance and ASA International India Microfinance exited the NBFI business. Two other companies — Shivam Securities and April Investment and Finance, surrendered their registrations after ceasing to exist as legal entities following amalgamation, merger, dissolution or voluntary strike-off.

The RBI said the remaining two cases were linked to companies meeting criteria under which separate NBFC registration was no longer required. Anagram Industries surrendered its registration after meeting the criteria prescribed for an unregistered Core Investment Company (CIC) that does not require registration. CDN Finance surrendered its certificate after meeting the criteria prescribed for an unregistered Type-I NBFC, which is also exempt from registration requirements.

The latest action follows several rounds of RBI decisions involving NBFC registrations this year, covering both regulatory cancellations and voluntary surrenders. The distinction between the two categories is significant. The five companies whose certificates were cancelled can no longer operate as NBFCs under the RBI registration granted to them, while the eight companies voluntarily surrendered their certificates for reasons including business exits, corporate restructuring and changes in their regulatory classification.

The RBI has been tightening oversight of the NBFC sector in recent years, with registration and compliance requirements forming an important part of its regulatory framework. The latest cancellations and surrenders therefore reflect both regulatory action and corporate restructuring, rather than a single reason for the exit of all 13 entities.
